channel.description: The news, verified. Independent geopolitical news.

item.title: The US-Israel war on Iran: reported US strikes hit Qeshm Island as Trump says a deal is coming together
item.description: The Wall Street Journal reported US strikes on Qeshm Island on Monday, described by US officials as limited and defensive against surface-to-air missile threats to US assets — no damage or casualty figure is verified — even as Trump said a deal was 'coming together very nicely'; Thursday brought a sharper split: Tehran warned any renewed US attack would bring 'long and painful strikes' on US regional positions, Axios reported Trump was briefed on further-strike plans, and Senator Blumenthal said an imminent strike was 'very much on the table' — while no strike decision is reported and the US proposal remains under review in Tehran. Thursday evening brought the post-midterm split into the open: Vance blamed the war for the defeat, Qalibaf mocked the post, and two Reuters sources said Trump was still likely to order renewed strikes — while no strike decision is reported. Overnight, Trump said a decision is coming — ‘You will know soon enough’ — and that US forces are ‘locked and loaded’; Reuters reported Iran has sent a nuclear proposal to Washington via Qatar, to be discussed only after the US meets Tehran’s seven demands. No strike order is reported. Trump also acknowledged on Thursday that 18 US service members have died in the conflict — his figure, not independently verified. Iraq's foreign minister warned on Thursday that the war 'has not stopped', and Fox News reported Trump met his security team to weigh resuming operations. Friday midday, Eurasia Group cut its estimated chance of renewed US strikes to 60% from 65% — but also cut the chance of a deal to 10% from 20%, raising a prolonged standoff to 30%. Friday afternoon, Iraq's prime minister told Trump in a Thursday call that Iraqi territory must not be used as a launch point for attacks on neighbours, as US envoy Tom Barrack met him in Baghdad. Friday afternoon also brought a Qatar track: Trump called Emir Sheikh Tamim, who pressed continued dialogue, avoiding escalation, freedom of navigation in Hormuz and secure energy supplies. Friday, the IRGC said it downed a US MQ-1 drone over Qeshm and two MQM-170 drones, Trump warned the US 'may have to destroy the rest of Iran', and Iraq proposed a regional foreign-ministers mission to Tehran and Washington. Overnight, Iranian media reported two missiles hit Qeshm Island with no casualties reported, Iran claimed an MQ-9 drone downed over the island, CENTCOM called the situation ‘relatively calm’ and said it would issue an announcement on Saturday morning, and Qatar denied reports that US-Iran talks had failed. Saturday morning, the Wall Street Journal reported Trump's advisers split — Hegseth and CENTCOM chief Cooper backing a return to major combat operations, Netanyahu still pushing renewed strikes — while Iranian officials are expected back in Doha as early as Saturday and the deal under discussion would cut preliminary talks from 60 days to two; the USS Theodore Roosevelt has reached Singapore and will not reach the region before mid-November. No strike decision is reported. Saturday morning, CENTCOM offered up to $20 million for information on Iran's nuclear programme, and Iran's army spokesman said Iranian forces are 'stronger' than at the war's start. Saturday morning, Qatar's prime minister said mediation continues, significant progress has been made and a settlement could be reached — 'We cannot wait to reach a perfect agreement; we hope to reach a good agreement' — while AP detailed the Qatari two-day 'bridge deal' (US lifts the blockade and releases frozen funds on day one; Iran reopens Hormuz under an Oman arrangement on day two), which Tehran is reviewing without yet accepting. Friday at the White House, Trump said 'We've beaten Iran' and that Hormuz was opening — a claim not independently confirmed — as Treasury sanctioned eight Canada-based firms accused of moving Iranian funds through crypto networks.

item.title: Saudi-led coalition launches large-scale operation against Ansar Allah as the Red Sea–Hormuz corridor tightens
item.description: Yemen's government forces say they recaptured positions in northern Lahij, a claim contested by Ansar Allah's earlier account of holding the al-Maqatirah ground — with no independent verification of who holds it — as the Red Sea–Hormuz corridor fighting continues. The Presidential Leadership Council claims about 20,000 Ansar Allah fighters were taken out of action in the offensive's first month — unverified, and at odds with the government's own earlier 16,100 figure. On Friday the coalition said it intercepted two ballistic missiles fired toward Najran — debris fell and damage is being assessed; the interception is the coalition's claim, not independently confirmed. Friday afternoon the coalition also said it intercepted a drone in the Makkah region — Ansar Allah denies targeting the holy city; the intercept is the coalition’s claim, not independently confirmed. Friday evening, airstrikes hit a crowded market in Taiz's al-Waziyah district, killing at least 20 people according to Ansar Allah's health ministry — but Taiz authorities deny any airstrikes took place and blame Ansar Allah; the Sanaa health ministry's cumulative toll rose to 276 killed and 654 wounded. Friday, Ansar Allah said it drove Saudi-backed Giants Forces brigades from the Kahbub heights near Bab al-Mandab, while Saba reported Saudi airstrikes on a crowded Taiz market killed and wounded more than 30 civilians. Overnight, the two sides traded blame for the Taiz market attack, and Riyadh denied a Wall Street Journal report that Ansar Allah demanded $51 billion to end hostilities. Saturday, the coalition said it intercepted a cruise missile toward Riyadh and a drone over the city late Friday, while government forces claimed gains in Taiz.

item.title: One year on, Gaza's promised 'day after' has not arrived — AP
item.description: A year after the US-brokered ceasefire took effect, all captives are home but Israel controls ~70% of Gaza, reconstruction has not begun, and strikes continue — medics report at least three Palestinians killed in Monday strikes in Khan Younis and Al-Mussadar, with a second agency reporting two. MSF analysis reported Thursday put hard numbers behind the malnutrition picture: in a 201-mother NICU cohort, more than half were malnourished during pregnancy, 90% of their babies were premature and 84% had low birth weight. Washington announced on Wednesday that the truce has entered Phase Two, and Netanyahu objected to the new Gaza Executive Board's composition. Friday, 15-year-old Mohammed Nidal Barbakh was shot dead at al-Mawasi, west of Khan Younis. Saturday, at least four more Palestinians were killed, including a teacher in Nuseirat, and the ministry's Saturday toll of 1,580 sits unreconciled against its Thursday total of 1,602.

item.title: Shipping and insurance markets are repricing the Strait of Hormuz
item.description: Brent settled Friday at $98.32 a barrel and WTI at $90.83 — down about 16% on the week from the previous Friday's $117.64, the steepest weekly fall since 2020 — even as the UN maritime chief reiterated on Monday that no one should transit the Strait of Hormuz, saying he cannot confirm mines have been cleared, disputing the US military's clearance claim. Friday midday, Brent traded $99.52–$100.75, still on course for a weekly fall of about 12–13%, as Eurasia Group cut both strike odds (60%) and deal odds (10%). Friday evening, India's HPCL said it is struggling to book tankers to lift crude through the strait even as flows recover — vessel availability, not crude supply, is the constraint, its chairman told Bloomberg. Iran's Hormuz blacklist was reshuffled to 239 vessels, and the IMO tracker lists 129 confirmed regional maritime incidents with 24 seafarer fatalities. The IRGC's Friday claim of two more tankers striking mines remains unconfirmed — CBS reported no confirmation from maritime officials. Reuters reported Friday that freight from the US Gulf Coast to Asia now costs $30-35 a barrel, against about $5 a year ago, handing Gulf Coast refiners an edge over Asian rivals as refining margins more than doubled. War-risk insurance for Hormuz transits has now reached 3% of hull value, twelve times the pre-war rate, BeInsure reported Friday.

item.title: US sanctions the entire ICC — Rubio vows to dismantle it 'brick by brick'
item.description: The US sanctioned the Hague court as an institution on Oct 9, hours after a former ICC judge won the Nobel Peace Prize — demanding the Netanyahu/Gallant warrants be dropped and issuing an April 2027 ultimatum. Canada, France, Germany, Japan and the UK rejected the move.

item.title: Russia is supplying missiles to Iran as Tehran rebuilds its arsenal, report says
item.description: A Reuters investigation traces how Iran keeps rebuilding missile and drone stocks through a 5,000-agency procurement network importing at least $2 billion of military-related goods since January 2025, despite the US naval blockade — the latest evidence of Tehran rebuilding its arsenal. Friday, The Telegraph reported, citing a high-ranking Iranian official, that Khamenei asked Putin to supply S-400 air-defence systems; Moscow's decision is unknown.

item.title: Trump and Putin struck a diesel deal to blunt Iran-war fuel prices
item.description: Over 300,000 metric tons of Russian fuel would flow under a temporary US sanctions lift, easing the price shock from the war on Iran — but analysts doubt it will be enough. Friday, the AP reported at least five of the tankers had turned away from US ports and none of the promised diesel had yet reached the United States.

item.title: Putin meets Pezeshkian in Ashgabat and pledges mediation
item.description: The Russian president met his Iranian counterpart ahead of the CIS summit, offering to mediate as the war on Iran grinds into its eighth month. Tehran has since rejected the mediation proposal, Iranian officials said, holding to its seven conditions for any talks.

item.title: G7 weighs a 100-million-barrel oil release to steady war-time markets
item.description: The G7's 100-million-barrel release is now being implemented through the IEA — Germany will release up to 15 million barrels, France announced a 10-million-barrel release, and Italy says it has met its 10-million-barrel commitment.

item.title: Treasury license would let Russian diesel flow through April 2027
item.description: The diesel deal's sanctions carve-out reportedly extends through April 2027 — turning a wartime fix into a year-plus arrangement.
